title: Computer-Use Agent Evaluated on OSWorld
tools: Python · OSWorld (desktop-task benchmark) · Claude · SubQ Snap decision model · Gemma 4 · OCR (optical character recognition) · Slurm on the OSU (Oregon State University) cluster · AWS (Amazon Web Services)
blurb: An agent that operates a Linux desktop; on 60 OSWorld (desktop task benchmark) tasks, a simple single-loop design scored 27, ahead of the planner stack's 16 and 20.
long: An agent that operates a real desktop from a plain-language goal. OCR (optical character recognition) turns each screenshot into numbered UI elements, a fast decision model picks the next action in about 0.5 s, and a vision model (Claude) takes over when it is unsure.
On 60 multi-app test tasks from OSWorld (a desktop-task benchmark), the decision model alone solved 0, and my planner stack solved 16 (v2) and 20 (v3), a gap within run-to-run noise.

Reading v3's failures showed the planner itself caused many of them, so I replaced it with one simple loop, which solved 27 of 60. I designed that loop after reading test failures, so the test set is no longer clean, and later changes used the dev tasks only.
highlights: 60 OSWorld (desktop-task benchmark) multi-app test tasks: decision model alone 0, stack v2 16, v3 20, one loop 27
v3 vs v2: p = 0.42 (exact McNemar test), within noise
Fast decider ~0.5 s per step; vision model ~5 s
OSWorld 2.0 sample: 0 of 10 fully completed, mean partial score 0.196
